full_judgment:
A.K.M. Shahidul Huq: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party no. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment " and decree dated 27.04.1998 and 30.04.1998 respectively passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, and Artho Rin Adalat Patuakhali, in Title Appeal no. 145 of 1996 allowing the appeal and reversing the Judgment and decree dated 14.10.1996 and 20.10.1996 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, in-charge Additional court, Patuakhali in Title Suit no. 18 of 1996 should not be set aside and/or to pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 7. During trial the plaintiffs examined 4 witnesses and defendant no.1 examined 4 witnesses and added defendant no. 12 examined 2 witnesses in support of their respective claim and after concluding trial the learned trial court by the judgment and decree dated 14.10.1996 and 20.10.1996 respectively decreed the suit on the ground that the plaintiff was found a regular teacher and selection of defendant no. 1 dated 11.12.1991 was not legal. 

 8. Against the judgment and decree the opposite party no:1 as appellant fled Title Appeal no. 145 of 1996 in the Court of District Judge, Patuakhali which was ultimately heard by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Patuakhali who by the judgment and decree dated 27.04.1998 and 30.04.1998 respectively allowed the appeal and send back the suit on remand to the learned trial court for retrial on the round that the circular no.  সাঃ ৭/৩ পি-২৭/৯০/৮২ শিক্ষা তারিখ ১৩.২.৯১ ইং/৩০.১০.৯৭ বাংলা Was not properly considered. 

 18. He also submits that during the trial the plaintiff examined 4 witnesses and defendant no. 1 examined 4 witnesses and added defendant no. 12 examined 2 witnesses in support of their respective claim and after concluding the learned trial court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 14.10.1996 and 20.10.1996 respectively decreed the suit are matter of record and but the statements stating that, "on the ground that the plaintiff was found a regular teacher and selection of the defendant no.1 dated 11.12.199 I was not legal" are illegal, wrong, misleading and misconstrued. With regard to the statements made in this paragraph under reference it is stated that the defendant opposite party no. I appointed as Assistant teacher in the said school on 25.05.1976 & joined on 01.06.1976 & worked as a regular teacher in this school. In 1991 when the government took the decision that the teachers of non-government primary schools shall be given grant, the plaintiff petitioner in collusion with the members of the Managing Committee of the school, entered the name of the plaintiff petitioner instead of defendant-opposite party no. 1 changing the registers and other documents of the school and created new documents in support of the service of the plaintiff-petitioner. The defendant-opposite party no.1 filed an application to the then State Minister for the Ministry of Education for taking action against the illegal activities of the plaintiff-petitioner & the then Managing Committee. The honourable Minister directed the Chairman of the District Selection Committee to enquire into the matter & to take proper action. The then Chairman of the district Selection committee, Mr. Moazzam Hossain Principal, PatuakhaIi government college along with secretary of the committee went to the locality on 09.10.1991 & enquired into the matter in presence of the teacher, members of the managing Committee & local elites. By the enqui9ry the allegations raised by the defendant-opposite party no. 1 as teacher no. 2 and the plaintiff petitioner as Teacher no. 5 in the report dated 11.12.1991 (exhibit no. IV). 

 19. He further submits that the suit of the plaintiff-respondent petitioner is not maintainable because the plaintiff respondent petitioner has/had no legal character for praying these declarations in this suit under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act; because the terms and conditions of the service of plaintiff petitioner are not regulated by any legal instrument (59 DLR 166) and as such the suit of the plaintiff respondent petitioner is not maintainable and the same should be dismissed and the rule of the civil revision is liable to be discharged with modification of the impugned judgment and decree o the appellate court not sending the same on remand. When the government took the decision that the teachers of the non-government primary schools shall be given grant, the plaintiff-petitioner in collusion with the members of the Managing committee of the School, entered his name instead of defendant-opposite party no. 1 changing the registers and other documents of the School and created new documents in support of the service of the plaintiff-petitioner. The defendant opposite party no. 1 filed all application to the then State Minister for the Ministry of Education for taking action against the illegal activities of the plaintiff petitioner & the then Managing Committee. The honourable Minister directed the Chairman of the District Selection Committee to enquire into the matter & to take proper action. The then Chairman of the district Selection Committee, Mr. Moazzam Hossain Principal, Patuakhali Government College along with secretary of the committee went to the locality on 09.10. I991 & enquired into the matter in presence of the Teachers, members of the Managing Committee & local elites. By the enquiry the allegations raised by the defendant opposite party no. 1 was proved and they found the defendant opposite party no.1 as teacher no. 2 and the plaintiff petitioner as Teacher no. 5 in the enquiry report dated 11. I 2.1991 (Exhibit no.) IV) and as such the suit of the plaintiff respondent petitioner is not maintainable and the same should be dismissed and the rule of the civil revision is liable to the discharged with modification of the impugned judgment and decree of the appellate court not sending the same on remand. 

 20. He lastly Submits that P.W 2 admitted in his cross-examination that no interview was held for the appointment of the plaintiff petitioner and he was the teacher no. 5 which proved that the enquiry report dated 11.12.1991 (Exhibit no. IV) is proper and as such the plaintiff petitioner cannot get the declaration as prayed for and as such the suit of the plaintiff respondent petitioner is not maintainable and the same should be dismissed and the rule of the civil revision is liable to he discharged with modification of the impugned judgment and decree of the appellate court not sending the same on remand. The appellate court found that the defendant opposite party no.1 was the teacher of the School, but the plaintiff petitioner could not proved by legal evidence that he was dismissed from his service and in the enquiry report dated 11.12.1991 (Exhibit no. IV) it is stated that,  বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের যেসকল মন্তব্য বই পাওয়া গিয়াছে তাহাতে জনাব মোঃ শাহ আলম খানের বিরুদ্ধে বিদ্যালয়ে অননুমোদিতভাবে অনুপস্থিত থাকা অথবা অন্য কোন কারণে কখনও কোন কৈফিয়ত তলব অথবা কোন বিধিগত ব্যবস্থা গ্রহনের কোন রেকর্ড নাই। এই বিষয়ে বিদ্যালয়ের প্রধান শিক্ষক এবং কমিটির সভাপতি ও অন্যান্য সদস্যবৃন্দকে জিজ্ঞাসাবাদ করিয়া জানা গেল যে, তাঁহার বিরুদ্ধে কখনও ঐ ধরনের ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করা হয় নাই। and as such the suit of the plaintiff respondent petitioner is not maintainable and the same should be dismissed and the rule of the civil revision is liable to be discharged with modification of the impugned judgment and decree of the appellate court not sending the same on remand. 

 22. I have perused the impugned judgment and decree of the last court of fact passed in title appeal no. 145 of 1996 perused the revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure also considered the submissions as advanced by the learned Advocate of both sides in support of their respective case. 

 25. From the defence taken by the defendant no. 1 in title suit no. 50 of 1984 as it is quire evident that right claimed by the plaintiffs under the agreement between the defendant no. 1 and plaintiffs is depended in the result of title Suit no. 360 of 1979. It is further seen that an order of injunction in Title suit no. 360 of 1979 is in force restraining the defendant no. 1 from dealing with the property in any manner and consequently if a decreed the affirmative is passed in title suit no. 50 of 1984 that would not become effective in disposal of the title suit no. 360 of 1979. In the background of the said undisputed facts the order of the High Court Division sending back the case on remand for trial of title suit no 50 of 1984 analogously with title suit no. 360 of 1979 can all together be not said justified even though has been made in the absence of prayed from the parties. It is now the settled principle of law that order of remand should not be made lightly by the superior court and that if materials on record are sufficient for the disposal of the suit in that case instead of sending of the suit back on remand the superior court should dispose of the same. The above is the general as well as broad principle of law but there may be case (s0 as the instant one, even though there is no prayer from the parties in the proceeding for sending the suit back to the trial court or to the lower appellate court for disposal where right of the parties to the proceeding so send back on remand is depended on the result of a suit filed earlier still remands pending the order of remand by the appellate/higher court made in such a situation cannot he considered unjustified. 

 33. In the result, the rule is made absolute, there will be no order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 27.4.1998 and 30.04.1998 respectively passed Subordinate Judge, and Artho Rin Adalat Patuakhali, in title appeal no. 145 of 1996 allowing the appeal and remanding the case to the learned trial court for re-trial by reversing the judgment and decree dated 14.10.1998 and 20.10.1996 respectively passed by learned Senior Assistant Judge, in charge Additional Court, Patuakhali in Title Suit no. 18 of 1996 is herby restored.
